subject: Economics
description: IRDAI, LIC, GIC, sectors, FDI limits, key schemes, recent reforms

questions.stem: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) was established under the:
questions.explanation: IRDA Act 1999 — set up IRDAI in April 2000 to regulate the insurance sector following its opening to private players (Malhotra Committee, 1994). Headquartered in Hyderabad. Renamed IRDAI in 2014. Issues licences, monitors solvency, prescribes rules, settles disputes. Reports to MoF. Currently chaired by Debasish Panda (since 2022). Insurance Act 1938 is the basic insurance legislation; LIC Act 1956 nationalised life insurance (245 private insurers merged into LIC).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: LIC of India was nationalised on:
questions.explanation: LIC Act 1956 — nationalised 245 private life insurers into LIC. Operations began 1 September 1956. Headquartered in Mumbai (Yogakshema Building). LIC IPO — May 2022 — government divested 3.5% stake; 2nd largest IPO ever in India (₹21,000 crore). Currently 32 life insurers in India (1 public + 31 private) and 26 general insurers + 4 specialised + several health insurers. General Insurance Corporation (GIC) — 1972, holds 4 subsidiaries (now separated): NIA, OIC, NIC, UIIC. Disinvested 2023.

questions.stem: FDI cap in insurance sector — most-recently set at:
questions.explanation: FDI history in insurance: 26% (2000, on opening), 49% (2015 Insurance Amendment Act), 74% (Budget 2021, Finance Act 2021). Up to 74% under automatic route, with conditions on Indian-controlled board. Insurance intermediaries (brokers, agents) → 100%. Lloyds India, reinsurance branches allowed. Budget 2024-25 hinted at allowing 100% FDI in insurance, possibly via Ins. Amendment Bill — under consideration.

questions.stem: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) — launched 2015 — provides life insurance cover of:
questions.explanation: PMJJBY — launched 9 May 2015. Life insurance cover ₹2 lakh, available to individuals 18-50 with savings bank account, paid via auto-debit. Annual premium ~₹436 (raised in 2022 from ₹330). Underwritten by LIC (also private insurers). PMSBY (Suraksha Bima Yojana) — accident + disability insurance ₹2 lakh, premium just ₹20/yr (raised from ₹12 in 2022). APY (Atal Pension Yojana) — pension scheme. Together — JANSURAKSHA suite providing financial security to underprivileged.

questions.stem: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — crop-insurance scheme launched 2016 — replaced:

options.option_text: NAIS (National Agricultural Insurance Scheme) and MNAIS

questions.explanation: PMFBY — launched 13 January 2016 (Sehore, MP). Replaced NAIS (1999) and MNAIS (2010). Aims to provide affordable crop insurance for farmers — premium just 1.5% (rabi), 2% (kharif), 5% (commercial) of insured sum; rest subsidised by Centre + State. AY 2020 — voluntary participation (was mandatory for loanee farmers earlier). Implemented by AIC (Agriculture Insurance Company of India) + private insurers. Covers natural calamities, pests, diseases. Around 5-6 crore farmers enrolled annually. PMFBY is the largest crop-insurance program in the world by area covered.

questions.stem: AYUSHMAN BHARAT — Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), launched 2018 — provides annual health cover up to:

options.option_text: ₹5 lakh per family per year (secondary + tertiary care)

questions.explanation: PM-JAY (launched 23 September 2018, Ranchi) — health cover ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary + tertiary care hospitalisation. Beneficiaries identified via SECC 2011 — ~10.74 crore poor + vulnerable families = ~50 crore people. World's largest government-funded health insurance scheme. Cashless + paperless treatment at ~28,000 empanelled hospitals (PMJAY portal). National Health Authority (NHA) implements. Senior citizens (70+) added September 2024 — irrespective of income/SECC eligibility.

questions.stem: Insurance penetration in India (premiums as % of GDP) currently is approximately:
questions.explanation: Insurance Penetration: Premiums / GDP. India's penetration (Swiss Re Sigma 2023): Total ~4.0%; Life ~3.0%; Non-life ~1.0%. Global average ~7% (advanced economies typically 8-10%). India ranks ~10th in life insurance worldwide by premium volume. Insurance density (premium per capita) much lower in India ($90) vs US ($8,000). IRDAI's 'Insurance for All by 2047' vision aims to dramatically raise penetration via simpler products, regulatory ease (Bima Sugam, Bima Vahak), and digital onboarding.

questions.stem: IRDAI shifted its permanent headquarters from New Delhi to which city in the year 2001?

options.option_text: Chennai — capital of Tamil Nadu state
Bengaluru — the Silicon Valley of India

questions.explanation: IRDAI was initially set up in Delhi (1999) but shifted to Hyderabad in 2001 as its permanent headquarters — Hyderabad was chosen partly for its central location and IT infrastructure. Mumbai is a common distractor because it hosts most financial regulators like SEBI, RBI, and stock exchanges, but IRDAI was deliberately placed elsewhere.

questions.stem: Which public sector undertaking is designated as the sole national reinsurer of India under the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act and its amendments?

options.option_text: General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)

questions.explanation: GIC Re (General Insurance Corporation of India) is the designated national reinsurer of India. When the insurance sector was opened to private players (post-1999 IRDA Act), GIC's four subsidiaries — New India, National, Oriental, United India — became independent direct insurers, while GIC was restructured exclusively as the country's reinsurer. New India Assurance is the largest general insurer but is NOT a reinsurer.

questions.stem: The annual premium under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) was revised upward from ₹12 to what amount in June 2022, while keeping the accidental death cover at ₹2 lakh?

options.option_text: ₹15 per year, covering accidental death only
₹20 per year, accidental death and disability
₹25 per year, covering accidental death only
₹36 per year, accidental death and disability

questions.explanation: PMSBY was launched in May 2015 at ₹12/year; the premium was revised to ₹20/year from June 2022 — the first revision in seven years. The scheme covers accidental death AND total permanent disability (₹2 lakh) and partial permanent disability (₹1 lakh). Candidates confuse ₹330, which is the PMJJBY (life insurance) premium, not PMSBY's rate.

questions.stem: A life insurance policy sold through 'distance marketing' (online/telephone) carries a free-look period of how many days under IRDAI regulations — longer than the standard free-look period?

options.option_text: 7 days from the date of receipt of the policy
15 days from the date of receipt of the policy
30 days from the date of receipt of the policy
45 days from the date of receipt of the policy

questions.explanation: IRDAI mandates a 15-day free-look period for standard life insurance policies, but this is extended to 30 days for policies sold through distance marketing (online, phone, courier) where the buyer cannot examine the product in person before purchase. 15 days is the most tempting distractor because it applies to offline/agent-sold policies — candidates often do not know the special 30-day rule for digital channels.

questions.stem: The Bima Lokpal (Insurance Ombudsman) scheme, which entertains policyholder complaints up to ₹50 lakh, is governed by rules notified by which authority?

options.option_text: IRDAI, under the Insurance Act 1938, Chapter VB
Ministry of Finance, under the Insurance Act 1938
Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Companies Act 2013
Reserve Bank of India — Integrated Ombudsman Scheme

questions.explanation: The Bima Lokpal Rules 2017 (replacing the 1998 Rules) are notified by the Central Government — specifically the Ministry of Finance — exercising powers under Section 114(1) of the Insurance Act 1938. IRDAI administers operational aspects but does NOT notify the rules. RBI's Integrated Ombudsman is a separate scheme covering banks and NBFCs — a common distractor because both are ombudsman models launched around the same period.

questions.stem: IRDAI's Surety Insurance Contracts Guidelines (January 2022) primarily aimed to benefit which sector by enabling insurers to replace bank guarantees required for large-scale contracts?

options.option_text: Export sector needing trade credit risk protection
Banking sector managing NPA risk via guarantees

questions.explanation: Surety insurance bonds back contractual obligations — if a contractor defaults on an infrastructure project (roads, ports, railways), the insurer pays the obligee (typically a government body). IRDAI issued these guidelines following NITI Aayog and Ministry of Finance recommendations to deepen infrastructure financing and reduce over-dependence on bank guarantees, which tie up credit limits. Export credit insurance (ECGC) and crop insurance (PMFBY) are separate products unrelated to surety bonds.

questions.stem: The Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015 amended Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938. What does it provide regarding a life insurance policy that has been in force for MORE than three years?

options.option_text: Insurer may reject claim only if nominee is untraceable
Insurer cannot question the policy on any ground whatsoever
Insurer may still contest fraud claims for three more years
Insurer can cancel policy if premium arrears exceed six months

questions.explanation: Pre-2015, Section 45 allowed insurers to contest a policy on grounds of fraud even after two years. The 2015 Amendment made policies completely incontestable after three years from commencement — the insurer CANNOT repudiate the claim on any ground, including deliberate fraud or misrepresentation. This was a landmark consumer-protection change. Option C is the most dangerous distractor: many candidates recall that 'fraud' was an exception before 2015 and assume it still allows a window — but post-amendment, the three-year bar is absolute.
